newsitem.title: GERMANY: Viag says 96 pretax profit to match 95 at least.
newsitem.headline: Viag says 96 pretax profit to match 95 at least.

text.p: German diversified industrial group Viag AG said on Friday that it expected full-year 1996 pre-tax profit to at least match the 1995 level.
Viag said pre-tax profit in the first nine months totalled 1.82 billion marks, unchanged from the year-earlier level, while sales were also unchanged at about 32 billion marks.
Viag -96 pretax profit to match 95 at least
In a statement, Viag said it expected structural improvements to offset the absence of one-off earnings which had boosted 1995 results.
The group noted that earnings had recovered from a first-half decline when group pre-tax profit fell 21 percent to 1.178 billion marks.
Viag said sales increased in its electricity activities as well as at fertiliser activities of its subsidiary SKW Trostberg, drinks packaging unit Schmalbach-Lubeca and in personal computer trading.
But sales fell at subsidiary VAW's aluminium and rolled products businesses and in Kloeckner & Co's steel trading business, Viag said.
"The operating profit, which serves as an internal guide, even improved substantially," Viag said.
In 1995, Viag earnings were inflated by income from the sale of its 43.4 percent stake in Germany's biggest paper maker PWA and other major changes in shareholdings.
